value.body:
Match seeds, decided by Jack Heart. His words: "To me it seems more natural to say there's a single match config that you give and then it gets some sort of reliably moving seed that has its own kind of meta seed or something. You pass a meta seed to initiate a matchup and then you have some known function to iterate on that seed for each match. Using that seed, that seed can then get plugged into determinizing a match config." On the restated model below: "yeah let's go with that".
Model: (1) a seating has one config, a specification that may have random parts (e.g. a random deck per seat); (2) a base seed plus a known function gives seed i for match i, independent of the players, shared by every seating and both seat orders, so different players face identical draws; (3) play receives match.seed and determinizes the config (e.g. deck choice, before the game) and the game from it, splitting it into independent streams (config, engine, each player); (4) "deal" stops being a concept: it is match index i, and more games means more indices. Match identity becomes (players, config, seed index) instead of (players, config, games). Today match.seed hashes the key including players (records.py:507), which is why Manabot carries a deal in its config. Stored results under old keys must stay readable. Docs (docs/evaluation.md Deal example) follow. No release.
